main_body: Hip-roofed thatched hut: a large straw roof slope (rows ~4-52) over a log-plank wall with a central doorway (rows ~52-78)
top_band: Golden-yellow thatch roof slope, rows ~5-52, lightest at the top and in bands, with a dark brown ridge line at rows 4-5. The hipped sides widen toward the eave.
evidence: Reading down the middle column: the roof is a thick sloped thatch surface with a trapezoid hip silhouette, the same construction as the reference houses. A bright eave band at rows ~48-52 is followed by a dark brown shadow line under the overhang, then the vertical plank wall below. The door has a timber frame, a dark inner edge and a stone threshold, so it reads as inset. The roof is the visible top surface, so the piece is not a front elevation.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 tones (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) with repeating strand-tick texture on each course. The outline is dark brown beside the straw and wood, not black. The plank wall has several brown tones and the round shields carry some detail. The wall's vertical planks are less speckled than the references' stone and plaster, and the dark doorway is a fairly flat area. Overall it is close to the reference in craft, only slightly thinner.
